# onpager_user (Data Source)

Read one OnPager user through authorized configuration reads. Absence, ambiguity and denied reads are errors. Reads never modify configuration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "onpager_user" "example" {
  # Selects a local credential, never an OIDC subject or display name.
  local_login = "operator"
}

output "user_id" {
  value = data.onpager_user.example.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `email` (String) Exact human email selector for local or OIDC users. Configure exactly one of `id`, `local_login` or `email`. The backend trims and Unicode case-folds this selector; ambiguous email matches fail. The original configured value is retained; maximum 4096 UTF-8 bytes.
- `id` (String) Stable OnPager UUID. Configure exactly one identity selector. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID; computed when another selector is configured.
- `local_login` (String) Exact local credential login selector; never an OIDC subject or display name. Configure exactly one of `id`, `local_login` or `email`. The backend trims and Unicode case-folds this selector. The original configured value is retained; maximum 4096 UTF-8 bytes.

### Read-Only

- `active` (Boolean) Observed active state. Inactive objects remain readable; this data source never changes their state.
- `display_name` (String) Observed public display name.
- `email_normalized` (String) Observed normalized human email, or an empty string when no email is stored. The private identity read requires tenant `users.read`.

## Selection

Configure exactly one of `id`, `local_login` or `email`. `local_login` selects a
local credential, rather than an OIDC subject or display name. OIDC identity
uses an issuer/subject pair and has no common login selector. Email can match
local or OIDC users and is not guaranteed to be unique.

The API normalizes local login and email selectors using its identity rules;
blank normalized identifiers are invalid. Selectors remain as configured in
Terraform state, and `email_normalized` contains the server's normalized value.

Login and email lookups use an exact server-side filter with `limit=2`. Zero
matches, multiple matches or `has_more` produce a diagnostic. Each filter value
is limited to 4096 UTF-8 bytes and the full JSON filter to 8192 bytes. UUID
selection reads the user directly and bypasses these filter limits. Substring
search and the public user lookup directory are not used.

The unique match is read directly by UUID before its metadata is returned.

## Read behavior

Reads identity metadata, including inactive users. Missing users, denied access,
malformed responses and transport failures produce diagnostics. Returned
identity metadata persists in Terraform state; credential values and bearer
tokens are excluded.

## Permissions

Requires the tenant grant `users.read` for personal tokens and service accounts.
The public directory grant `lookups.read` does not authorize private identity
selectors.
